sections.normalized_html: A tank is being filled with water. What is an appropriate unit for measuring the rate of change of water volume in the tank, as time goes on?
sections.readable_text: A tank is being filled with water. What is an appropriate unit for measuring the rate of change of water volume in the tank, as time goes on?

sections.normalized_html:
We measure the change of the volume as we change the amount of time. Consequently, any appropriate unit for measuring the rate of change of water volume in the tank must take the form [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{unit of volume}}{\textrm{unit of time}}.]

Some examples of appropriate units include [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{liters}}{\textrm{hour}},] [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{m}^3}{\textrm{min}},] and [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{cm}^3}{\textrm{s}}.]

items.title: Choosing Appropriate Units When Base Units Are Required

sections.normalized_html: Density [MATH: D] is the rate that mass [MATH: M] changes as volume [MATH: V] changes. What are the units of density in terms of base units?

sections.normalized_html:
We measure the change in the mass, as we change the volume. Consequently, any appropriate unit must take the form [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{unit of mass}}{\textrm{unit of volume}}.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Sometimes, when we are choosing an appropriate unit, we are not given any formula to use.

Content:
This often occurs when we measure the rate of change of something. A rate of change measures how much something changes as we change something else.

Content:
In such cases, we can use a quotient to work out an appropriate unit. The numerator is what we measure the change of, and the denominator is what we change:
[MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}\textrm{what we measure the change of}}{\color{red}\textrm{what we change}}]

Content:
For instance, suppose that a newly opened store wants to measure the rate at which the number of customers increases each day.

Content:
We measure the change of the number of customers, as we change the number of days, so the most appropriate unit is
[MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}\textrm{customers}}{\color{red}\textrm{day}},]
or, customers per day.

Some examples of appropriate units include [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{liters}}{\textrm{hour}},] [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{m}^3}{\textrm{min}},] and [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{cm}^3}{\textrm{s}}.]
